title: Topology and open substacks of a Deligne--Mumford stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$, with stack, atlas, representability and 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Define $|\mathcal X|$ to be the set of maps $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$ from fields modulo the equivalence relation that two maps become 2-isomorphic over a common field extension. Give it the topology in which $W\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ is open precisely when its inverse image in an etale surjective scheme atlas $A\to\mathcal X$ is open in $|A|$; this is independent of the atlas. For a scheme this is its usual topological space. An open substack is a strictly full substack $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal X$ whose 2-base change by every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ is an open subscheme of $T$. The assignment $\mathcal U\mapsto|\mathcal U|\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ is an inclusion-preserving bijection from open substacks to open subsets. For every morphism $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ of Deligne--Mumford stacks and every open substack $\mathcal U$, the open substack $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$ corresponds to the subset $|f|^{-1}(|\mathcal U|)$ of $|\mathcal Y|$.

source.place: Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks); Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points); Tag 04XG (definition-points) and Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian) for the field-point and inverse-image conventions. Restricted to Deligne--Mumford stacks.

proof.text: The common-extension relation is reflexive and symmetric. For transitivity, suppose representatives $x/K$ and $y/L$ become isomorphic over $E$, and $y/L$ and $z/N$ become isomorphic over $F$. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to the extensions $E/L,F/L$, obtaining embeddings into $M$ agreeing on $L$. Pull the two isomorphisms to $M$ and compose them through the common pullback of $y$. This gives the required isomorphism between $x|_M$ and $z|_M$. Pullback and composition here are those of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Thus the quotient defining points exists in the standing universe.

For a scheme $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] identifies a map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ with a point $t$ and an embedding $\kappa(t)\to K$. Equivalent maps have the same image point. Conversely, two maps with image $t$ become equal over a common extension of their fields over $\kappa(t)$, by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields]. Every point is represented by its residue-field map. This gives a canonical bijection between the field-point quotient and the ordinary point set of $T$, compatible with scheme morphisms.

Postcomposition sends an isomorphism after a common field extension to another such isomorphism, so every stack morphism induces a well-defined map on points. For a 2-fibre product $\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y$, two field representatives whose images in $|\mathcal X|$ coincide have, by definition, pullbacks over a common field with an isomorphism between those images. The triple of these two pullbacks and that isomorphism is an object of the 2-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Consequently its point set surjects onto $|\mathcal Z|\times_{|\mathcal X|}|\mathcal Y|$. Only surjectivity is asserted: different comparison isomorphisms need not give the same point.

Let $p:A\to\mathcal X$ be the given etale surjective atlas. For a field object $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$, its pullback $E=A\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a surjective algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ by the atlas convention [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Take a surjective etale scheme cover $C\to E$ as supplied by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Apply the current chart-test equivalence in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] to the representable surjective map $E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and its chosen surjective etale scheme chart $C\to E$. It says exactly that the scheme map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is surjective. Since its target has a point, choose a point of $C$ and its residue-field map. Writing $L$ for that residue field, step 2 applied to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ gives the embedding $K\to L$. The resulting field object of $E$ is a triple: an $L$-object of $A$ and an isomorphism to $x|_L$. Thus $|p|$ is surjective. The same argument applies to any representable surjective scheme-source morphism. With $R=A\times_{\mathcal X}A$, step 3 now shows that the image of $|R|\to |A|\times|A|$ is exactly the relation of having the same image in $|\mathcal X|$.

For another etale surjective scheme atlas $A'\to\mathcal X$, put $E=A\times_{\mathcal X}A'$. Both projections are etale and surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Choose a surjective etale scheme cover $C\to E$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Composition gives etale surjective scheme maps $a:C\to A$ and $b:C\to A'$. Here ordinary scheme surjectivity follows from the same node's chart test, applied to each representable surjective projection $E\to A$ or $E\to A'$ with chart $C\to E$ and the identity scheme base change. They are continuous, since scheme morphisms are morphisms of locally ringed spaces [def-pc-scheme], and open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. A continuous open surjection $q$ detects openness: $q^{-1}(V)$ open implies $V=q(q^{-1}(V))$ open, and continuity proves the converse. The inverse images on $C$ of $|p|^{-1}(W)$ and $|p'|^{-1}(W)$ coincide. Hence these subsets are open simultaneously, proving atlas independence. For each atlas the prescribed opens form a topology, since inverse image preserves arbitrary unions and finite intersections.

source.place: Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points), first paragraph; scheme openness Tag 03WT

proof.text: The topology just constructed agrees with a scheme's topology: use its identity atlas and the point bijection of step 2. More generally, for any scheme map $T\to\mathcal X$ and open $W\subseteq|\mathcal X|$, cover $T\times_{\mathcal X}A$ by a surjective etale scheme $C$ [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Its composite $C\to T$ is etale surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]: etaleness uses base change and composition, and ordinary scheme surjectivity uses the chart test for $T\times_{\mathcal X}A\to T$ with chart $C$. It therefore is an open continuous surjection by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map, def-pc-scheme]. The inverse image of $W$ on $C$ is the inverse image of the open $|p|^{-1}(W)$ under the scheme morphism $C\to A$, hence open. Openness descends to $T$ by the calculation in step 5. This also proves continuity for a morphism of DM stacks by testing its composite with an atlas of its source.

Write $s,t:R\to A$ for the atlas relation. Subsets of $|\mathcal X|$ correspond to subsets $V\subseteq|A|$ saturated under equality of their images, by surjectivity in step 4: the maps are $W\mapsto|p|^{-1}(W)$ and $V\mapsto|p|(V)$. Saturation is equivalent to $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$ on point sets, by step 3 and the description of the relation in step 4. For open $V$, view it as its open subscheme of $A$. Its two pullbacks are open subspaces of $R$. Their point images are $|s|^{-1}(V)$ and $|t|^{-1}(V)$: projection gives one containment, and step 3 lifts a pair of representatives with equal image after a common extension for the reverse containment. These open subspaces are equal precisely when their point sets are equal, by the open-subspace classification in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Thus the open subsets of $|\mathcal X|$ correspond exactly to invariant open subschemes of $A$.

An etale atlas is smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] to $p:A\to\mathcal X$. Its hypotheses hold because a DM stack has representable diagonal and this smooth surjective scheme atlas. It gives an inclusion-preserving bijection between open substacks $\mathcal U$ and invariant open subschemes $V=A\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$. Compose it with step 7's bijection. If $\mathcal U_1\subseteq\mathcal U_2$, their atlas pullbacks satisfy $V_1\subseteq V_2$ by the inclusion-preserving clause of descent, and $|p|(|V_1|)\subseteq|p|(|V_2|)$ by direct image of subsets. Hence the composite preserves inclusion. It remains to identify its assigned subset with $|\mathcal U|$.

For a strictly full substack, two field objects in $\mathcal U$ which become isomorphic in $\mathcal X$ over an extension are already isomorphic in $\mathcal U$ there. Hence $|\mathcal U|\to|\mathcal X|$ is injective. Step 3 applied to $V=A\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$ gives $|V|=|p|^{-1}(|\mathcal U|)$ as subsets of $|A|$: one inclusion follows by projection, and a pair with equal images lifts to a field object of $V$ for the other. Since $|p|$ is surjective, $|p|(|V|)=|\mathcal U|$. This identifies the bijection in step 8 with the assignment in the statement and proves both its surjectivity and injectivity.

proof.text: For $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$, put $\mathcal V=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, associativity of the triple description of 2-fibre products identifies $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal V$ with $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$, an open subscheme of $T$. Thus $\mathcal V$ is the open substack obtained by pullback (take its strictly full essential image). Its point image is $|f|^{-1}(|\mathcal U|)$: projection proves containment; if a field representative in $\mathcal Y$ has image in $|\mathcal U|$, choose a representative in $\mathcal U$ and an isomorphism after a common extension; the resulting triple is a point of $\mathcal V$. Strict fullness makes its map to $|\mathcal Y|$ injective as in step 9. The already proved classification therefore assigns exactly the asserted inverse image to this open substack.
